one_liner: Senior Executive Service deputy to FHWA's CFO, running the agency's budget formulation and execution, accounting systems, audits, and allocation of Federal-aid highway funds.
fit_summary: This is an SES role that requires executive-level budget, accounting, and financial-management leadership, including managing multiple fund types and leading a financial organization (TQ 1 and TQ 2). Nothing on file shows Daniel has senior financial-management or executive supervisory experience. Daniel's policy knowledge fits ECQ 1, but that cannot offset missing TQs, and a QRB must certify the selectee's executive qualifications.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths: public, SES); you must be a U.S. citizen or national, and no prior federal status is needed.
You must show both Technical Qualifications (executive-level budget, financial, and accounting experience, and leading a high-performing financial management organization) in your resume.
You must address all five Executive Core Qualifications within a resume of no more than 2 pages; separate narratives are not accepted.
A Secret clearance is required (the posting also lists Confidential); expect a background investigation and fingerprinting.
You will need OPM QRB certification before appointment and must complete a one-year SES probationary period.
strategy: Be honest about whether you have actually led a budget or finance organization; if you have not, use this posting to learn what SES finance roles require rather than investing heavily in it.
If you apply, frame any IEM work on disaster recovery grants, FEMA Public Assistance, or cost tracking as financial stewardship, using [your actual role and dollar amounts].
Address each ECQ and TQ in compact bullets within 2 pages, with dates and hours per week; ECQ 1 is where your policy and constitutional knowledge can stand out.
Preview the vacancy questions early, answer them truthfully, and submit by 11:59 PM EST on November 6, 2026 (it opens October 7, 2026).

Run a parallel search for GS-9/11/12 budget analyst, program analyst, or emergency management specialist roles at DOT, FEMA, or DHS, plus legislative or Prince William County and Manassas positions that fit your background.
resume_bullets: Managed [type] budget of $[amount] for [government client] disaster recovery program at IEM, tracking [fund sources] and reconciling expenditures to [federal grant requirements], [hours/week].
Built partnerships with [number] [state/local/federal] stakeholders to resolve [specific funding or compliance issue], resulting in [verified outcome].
Led team of [number] staff to deliver [project] on schedule and [within/under] budget by [specific process improvement].
interview_questions: Describe a time you resolved a complex budget issue involving multiple fund types or appropriations constraints.
How have you driven efficiency or cut wasteful spending in an organization you led?
Tell us about holding staff accountable while leading people through organizational change.
How would you serve as the agency's point of contact for financial audit findings?
watch_outs: The executive-level finance requirements likely disqualify you without a substantial budget or accounting leadership record.
A resume over 2 pages will not be read past page 2 and may be disqualified, and narratives are rejected.
You must be able to obtain a Secret clearance, and the role includes a one-year probation requiring written certification for continued employment.
Selection may include a writing sample and a scenario-based presentation.
